item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
Mixed, leaning no. The 2024 record shows real anti-corruption and anti-favoritism rhetoric, plus some corrective policy moves, but the stronger pattern is Party capture of state machinery, politically conditioned regulation, and weak evidence that Xi’s system cleanly separates private interests from state power.

**Supports Yes**
| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Xi delivers important speech at CCDI plenary session | English.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-01-10 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202401/10/content_WS659dd697c6d0868f4e8e2e74.html | Xi publicly said corruption remained serious in finance, SOEs, energy, medicine, and infrastructure and called for tighter oversight. This is evidence of acknowledging and policing state-business corruption rather than openly tolerating it. | 7B.3, 5B.5 |
| China to defuse risks in real estate, local gov't debt, small and medium financial institutions | English.www.gov.cn / Xinhua | 2024-03-05 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202403/05/content_WS65e67f6ec6d0868f4e8e4a72.html | The work report openly named real-estate, local-debt, and financial-sector risks to the legislature. That is consistent with at least some separation of policy from vested interests, because the center acknowledged problems instead of masking them. | 7B.3, 7B.2, 6B.5 |
| China’s finance ministry pushed broad-based growth package | Xinhua / english.www.gov.cn | 2024-03-25 | https://english.www.gov.cn/news/202403/25/content_WS6600afebc6d0868f4e8e569e.html | The package promised fair treatment for all firms in tax relief and procurement, plus more spending on education, healthcare, social security, and environmental protection. That points to some anti-favoritism and non-captive policy design. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| NDRC says it will help private enterprises and protect entrepreneurs’ rights | Xinhua / english.news.cn | 2024-01-10 | https://english.news.cn/20240110/78198229d70d4ad2824f8b50c3bedeee/c.html | Beijing said it would support private firms, protect entrepreneurs’ rights, and use private-sector feedback in macro policy. This is at least a formal signal against pure crony capture. | 7B.3, 6B.10 |
| China orders heavily indebted local governments to halt some unfinished infrastructure projects | Reuters | 2024-01-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/exclusivechina-orders-indebted-local-governments-to-halt-some-infrastructure-projectssources-3277972 | Cutting or pausing projects after overborrowing is evidence of a corrective move against politically driven spending and local-capture excesses. | 7B.3, 6B.5, 6B.6 |
| Growth rises after investigations of connected officials | European Journal of Political Economy | 2024-06-01 | https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S017626802400051X | The paper finds growth increased after investigations of connected officials, consistent with anti-rent enforcement having real economic effects. This supports the idea that anti-corruption can reduce capture, though it does not prove Xi himself was cleanly separated from interests. | 7B.3, 5B.5 |

**Supports No**

|---|---|---:|---|---|---|

| Watchdog doubles down on Xi’s anti-graft drive | Reuters / MarketScreener | 2024-01-10 | https://hk.marketscreener.com/news/latest/China-watchdog-doubles-down-on-vow-to-heed-Xi-s-anti-graft-drive-45713924/ | The anti-graft apparatus said it would heed Xi’s drive to catch “corrupt and disloyal” officials. That suggests anti-corruption also functioned as loyalty enforcement, not just neutral conflict-of-interest control. | 7B.3, 5B.5, 7B.2 |
| China targets financial sector with Party-led anti-graft committee | Reuters / MarketScreener | 2024-07-24 | https://hk.marketscreener.com/news/latest/China-targets-financial-sector-with-party-led-anti-graft-committee-47453350/ | Reuters reported a new financial-sector anti-graft committee with political supervision and “party building” duties, showing finance was still being governed through Party control rather than insulated rules. | 7B.3, 5B.5, 6B.9 |
| Hong Kong national security law broadens sabotage, sedition, and state-secrets offenses | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxscope-of-hong-kongs-new-national-security-laws-3344082 | The law expanded the state’s coercive toolkit in ways that can protect regime interests rather than separate them from law enforcement. | 7B.3, 6B.9, 7B.2 |
| Hong Kong’s landmark national security trial for 47 democrats | Reuters | 2024-05-30 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/hong-kongs-landmark-national-security-trial-for-47-democrats-3462427 | Reuters reported long pretrial detention, bail denial, a juryless trial, and mass convictions, indicating courts were used for political punishment rather than neutral rule enforcement. | 7B.3, 7B.2, 6B.9 |
| Article 23 safety concerns forced RFA to close its Hong Kong bureau | Radio Free Asia | 2024-03-29 | https://www.rfa.org/english/news/china/rfa-bureau-closure-03292024133320.html/ | The closure of an independent bureau after security-law expansion shows state regulation and law enforcement were used to chill scrutiny, not stay separated from political interest. | 7B.3, 7B.2, 6B.9 |
| Religious venues required to indoctrinate CCP ideology and receive state-approved funding | Human Rights Watch | 2024 | https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/china | HRW described political conditioning of institutional support, which is a direct example of state resources being tied to Party loyalty rather than separated from it. | 7B.3, 6B.9, 7B.2 |
| China’s military elite purge reflects serious corruption inside the Rocket Force | Reuters / SCMP | 2024-07-18 | https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3270993/chinas-communist-party-targets-another-pla-general-corruption-investigation?UUID=f0bc4b91-7818-4f96-bf67-aa5b46ac9395&next_article_id=3270939&tc=7&tpcc=enlz-globalimpact | The purge of senior Rocket Force figures shows high-value security institutions remained vulnerable to opaque internal networks and loyalty politics, not cleanly insulated governance. | 7B.3, 5B.5, 6B.9 |
| Beijing framed Taiwan drills as “punishment” for “separatist acts” | Reuters | 2024-05-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-launches-war-games-around-taiwan-3453328 | The drills were framed as punitive political signaling, showing foreign policy and military power being used to serve regime narratives, not separated from them. | 7B.3, 7B.1, 6B.9 |

**Search Gap**  
I did not find credible 2024 public evidence that directly traces Xi’s personal family holdings, private business stakes, or formal recusal/asset-disclosure behavior. The strongest evidence is indirect and structural: Party control over the cabinet, loyalty-based anti-graft enforcement, politicized finance, and security-law repression. That means the record supports a “systemic capture” reading more strongly than a provable personal-family-conflict finding.
